title: SQLite: invalid create table DDL when schemaGenerator.createForeignKeyConstraints is disabled
body:
### Describe the bug

With `schemaGenerator: { createForeignKeyConstraints: false }`, the SQLite driver generates invalid `create table` DDL for entities with relations. Every foreign key adds an empty item to the column list:

```sql
create table `book` (`id` integer not null primary key autoincrement, `author_id` integer not null, `editor_id` integer not null, , );
```

So `orm.schema.create()` / `refresh()` fails with `near ",": syntax error`.

Expected:

```sql
create table `book` (`id` integer not null primary key autoincrement, `author_id` integer not null, `editor_id` integer not null);
```


### Reproduction

https://github.com/jbl428/reproduction (`src/create-foreign-key-constraints.test.ts`)

Minimal setup: two `@ManyToOne` relations, in-memory SQLite, `createForeignKeyConstraints: false`. The `current behavior` tests assert the broken output and the `expected behavior` tests fail until the bug is fixed.


### What driver are you using?

@mikro-orm/sqlite

### MikroORM version

7.2.3

### Node.js version

v22.22.3, TypeScript 5.8

### Operating system

macOS 26.6.2
